payload.title: AI Builders Daily · 2026-06-13
payload.summary:
**Coding agents crossed into real work**; cost, access, and regulation are suddenly the fight, from Fable restrictions to talk of ID-gated frontier models; **Anthropic spent the cycle fixing Claude Code and hardening Managed Agents**; X felt like a live wire: merge-conflict heresy, tokenmaxxing backlash, founder-brand advice, and a lot of people realizing attention is now the real bottleneck.

**能干活的 coding agent 已经不是演示了**；这两天吵得最凶的不是能力上限，而是谁能用、要花多少钱、政府准备管到哪一步；**Anthropic 一边给 Claude Code 擦屁股，一边把 Managed Agents 往企业内网里塞**；X 上也挺真实：有人嫌 Git 这套该退休了，有人拿 Fable 限制开火，还有人直说现在最稀缺的不是模型，是注意力。

sections.headline: **Coding agents grow up, open models look shakier, and API economics get weird / Coding agent 开始真干活，开源模型前景发虚，API 生意也变得别扭**
sections.body:
Jacob Efron, Ari from **Datalogy**, and Rob from **Radical** run a broad AI check-in and land on three big themes: coding agents are finally useful over longer time horizons, engineering teams are drifting toward managing fleets of agents instead of doing every step by hand, and the new bottleneck is no longer raw code generation but review, comprehension, and cleanup. They also argue that frontier open-weight AI may be entering a weaker phase as labs pull back for economic and geopolitical reasons.

The episode also leans hard into cost pressure. As models think longer and token bills jump, enterprises are pushing for cheaper and more efficient setups, even when they still want frontier-level results. One especially spicy claim: if compute stays tight, labs may eventually decide the API business itself is the wrong business to be in.

Jacob Efron、**Datalogy** 的 Ari 和 **Radical** 的 Rob 做了一次大盘点，核心就三件事：coding agent 终于开始能扛更长链路的活；很多工程师的日常正在从亲手写代码，慢慢变成同时盯几只 agent；真正卡人的地方也变了，不再是“能不能生成”，而是审查、理解和收拾残局。他们还提到，前沿开源权重模型这条线可能没前两年那么热了，经济账和地缘因素都在逼实验室收手。

另一个刺点是成本。模型思考时间一拉长，token 账单就跟着炸，企业端现在明显更在意性价比，不会再无脑往最贵那档冲。节目里最猛的判断是：如果算力一直这么紧，实验室最后连 API 这门生意都可能嫌麻烦。

sections.headline: **Anthropic explains the Claude Code quality dip and reverses three bad changes / Anthropic 拆解 Claude Code 质量下滑：三处改动翻车，现已回滚**
sections.body:
**Anthropic** says recent complaints about worse **Claude Code** behavior came from three product-layer changes, not the API or inference stack. The main culprits were a lower default reasoning setting, a caching bug that repeatedly dropped prior reasoning after idle sessions, and a prompt tweak aimed at cutting verbosity that ended up hurting coding quality. All three issues were fixed by April 20, and the company reset subscriber usage limits.

The post matters because it puts real mechanics behind vague "the model got worse" complaints. Anthropic’s takeaway is blunt: defaults, context handling, and prompt shaping can quietly degrade a coding product even when the underlying model is unchanged. They also note that **Opus 4.7** found the offending bug in back-tested code review while **Opus 4.6** did not.

**Anthropic** 的说法很直接：最近大家觉得 **Claude Code** 变笨，不是底层 API 或推理层出了事，而是产品层三处改动一起踩雷。一个是默认 reasoning effort 从高档降到了中档；一个是缓存优化写崩了，闲置会话恢复后会反复丢掉旧的思考链；还有一个是为了少说废话加的 system prompt，结果把写代码质量一并打掉了。这三处都在 4 月 20 日前修好，订阅用户的额度也重置了。

这篇的价值在于，它把那种空泛的“怎么感觉模型变差了”落回了具体工程问题。结论也不花哨：默认参数、上下文处理、提示词收口，这些看着像边角料，真能把 coding 体验拖垮。文里还提到一个细节：回头拿 **Opus 4.7** 做 code review 复盘时，它能抓到那次 bug，**Opus 4.6** 抓不到。

sections.headline: **Managed Agents splits the brain, hands, and memory to make long-running agents recoverable / Managed Agents 把“大脑、手、记忆”拆开，长时 agent 才真正稳得住**
sections.body:
**Anthropic** describes **Managed Agents** as a hosted system built around three separable interfaces: the session log, the harness, and the sandbox. That separation lets agent runs survive crashes, restart cleanly, and swap infrastructure without rewriting the whole stack. The design is framed less as a model trick and more as an old systems problem: build abstractions that keep working even as the implementation underneath changes.

A big practical payoff is security and reliability. By moving the harness outside the execution container and treating sandboxes as disposable cattle instead of precious pets, Anthropic says failures become easier to recover from and secrets stop living next to model-generated code. The session log also becomes a durable external memory, so long-horizon work is not trapped inside a single shrinking context window.

**Anthropic** 这篇写得挺系统：**Managed Agents** 不是简单把模型包一层，而是硬拆成三个接口来做，会话日志、harness、sandbox 各管各的。这样一来，agent 跑长任务时就算中间崩了，也能从日志里接着醒过来；底下换实现、换环境，也不用把整套东西推倒重来。它本质上更像系统设计题，不是什么花哨 prompt 技巧。

最实在的收益是稳和安全。harness 从容器里搬出去后，sandbox 挂了就按工具调用失败处理，重建一个新的就行，不用把旧容器当宠物救。另一刀也很关键：别再让模型生成的代码和凭证待在一个地方。再配上独立的 session log，长链路任务的记忆也不必硬塞进那点上下文窗口里。

sections.headline: **Claude Managed Agents adds self-hosted sandboxes and private MCP tunnels / Claude Managed Agents 上线自托管沙箱和私有 MCP 隧道**
sections.body:
**Claude Managed Agents** can now run tool execution inside customer-controlled sandboxes and reach private **MCP** servers through outbound tunnels. Anthropic keeps the orchestration loop, while execution, files, packages, and internal services stay inside the customer perimeter or a managed sandbox provider like **Cloudflare**, **Daytona**, **Modal**, or **Vercel**.

The update is squarely aimed at enterprises that want agent behavior without shipping sensitive infrastructure into a third-party runtime. Self-hosted sandboxes are in public beta, while MCP tunnels are in research preview, giving teams a cleaner path to connect agents to internal databases, APIs, and knowledge systems without exposing them on the public internet.

**Claude Managed Agents** 现在能把工具执行放进客户自己控制的沙箱里，还能通过私有 **MCP** 隧道去连内网服务。Anthropic 继续管 agent loop、上下文和恢复逻辑，但文件、依赖、仓库、内部服务这些东西，可以留在你自己的边界内，或者放到 **Cloudflare**、**Daytona**、**Modal**、**Vercel** 这类托管沙箱上。

这次更新很明显是冲企业场景去的：你想要 agent，但不想把敏感系统裸奔给第三方运行时。自托管沙箱已经进 public beta，MCP tunnels 还在 research preview，不过方向很清楚，就是让 agent 安静地吃到企业内网里的数据库、API、知识库，又不用把这些接口直接暴露到公网。

sections.headline: **What if Git is the next thing to break / 如果下一个该退休的是 Git 呢**
sections.body:
## The Future Codebase

After the PR dies, after the Code Review dies,
i am seriously wondering if Git needs to die next.

roughly 20-40% of code spend is just managing and updating merge conflicts. necessary evil? or legacy "horseless carriage"? cargo culting the past?

we don't do line by line merge conflicts when we collaborate with human colleagues - instead we chat, suggest edits, do side comments, and an owner ships it. 

btw we also don't do CI/CD even collaborating on documents with serious legal/financial implications.

maybe the future codebase looks more like a Notion or Linear database than .git objects. It will be less efficient, but more scalable. exactly the Salty Lesson.

## 未来的代码库

等 PR 这套死掉、Code Review 这套也死掉之后，
我很认真地在想，下一个该死的是不是 **Git**。

大概 20% 到 40% 的代码成本，其实都砸在处理和更新 merge conflict 上。它到底是必要之恶，还是一种“无马马车”式的遗留系统？只是习惯性地膜拜旧时代？

人和人协作时，并不会逐行解决冲突。我们会聊天、提建议、留边注，最后由 owner 发版。

顺便说一句，哪怕是协作那些有严肃法律或财务后果的文档，我们也不是靠 CI/CD 在干活。

未来的代码库，也许会更像 **Notion** 或 **Linear** 的数据库，而不是 `.git` objects。效率可能更低，但扩展性反而更强。很 **Salty Lesson**。

sections.headline: **He sees a real AI regulation turning point / 他认为 AI 监管真的到了转折点**
sections.body:
This is a big turning point for AI regulation.

The government is starting to deem some models too powerful for certain uses, which creates a precedent for a range of possible controls in the future.

I’m in the camp that this is unnecessary and we should be primarily regulating the use of AI, as opposed to the underlying models. But, equally, there are plenty of people that actually prefer this outcome.

Either way, it’s unlikely that we’re going back to a world where the government doesn’t have far more meaningful involvement in the rate of AI progress.

这对 AI 监管来说是个很大的转折点。

政府开始认定某些模型对某些用途来说“过于强大”，这等于为未来一整套可能的管制方式开了先例。

我站在另一边：我觉得这没必要，监管重点应该放在 AI 的使用方式上，而不是模型本身。当然，也确实有不少人更想看到现在这个结果。

不管怎样，想回到那个政府对 AI 进展速度没什么实质介入的世界，基本不太可能了。

sections.body:
Everyone thinks AI coding tools set founders free.

Watch what people actually build with them: rules, approvals, process, layers. The same cage, assembled faster.

The tool that can scaffold anything in an afternoon will scaffold your bureaucracy in an afternoon too.

Speed of construction is speed of calcification. Build the thing that lets you create new things: experiences that didn’t happen before.

所有人都以为 AI coding tools 会把创始人解放出来。

但你真去看大家拿它们做了什么：规则、审批、流程、层层包裹。同一个笼子，只是搭得更快了。

一个下午能把任何东西 scaffold 出来的工具，同样也能在一个下午把你的官僚体系 scaffold 出来。

建得越快，固化得也越快。去做那种能让你创造新东西的东西，做以前根本不会发生的体验。

sections.headline: **He says he writes with two distinct voices / 他说自己写字和说话时像是两种声线轮流上场**
sections.body:
Anyone else have two voices?

I often have two voices that come out both in my writing and how I speak. 

One is the frenetic, time is the enemy, direct, punchy gets to the point quickly and then the second is more calm, measured, structured inquisitive, trying to peel the layers. 

They are distinctive enough that people think it’s two different people (especially in writing). 

They are usually separate but I feel I often oscillate between the two in the same conversation.

还有谁也会这样，有两种声音吗？

我经常在写作和说话时都冒出两种不同的声线。

一种很躁，觉得时间是敌人，直接、猛、很快切进重点；另一种则更平静、更克制、更讲结构，也更爱追问，想把一层层东西剥开。

它们差别大到别人会以为那是两个人，尤其在文字里更明显。

平时这两种状态大多分开，但我感觉自己也常常会在同一场对话里来回切。

sections.headline: **Codex inside crabbox is becoming core infrastructure / 跑在 crabbox 里的 **Codex** 正在变成他的核心基础设施**
sections.body:
I can barely keep up with implementing/testing/landing all the Issues/PRs folks submit to https://t.co/qUxn0LF7Ct

Codex runs INSIDE crabbox while it is building crabbox.
This is becoming essential infra for my work.

Codex been looping nonstop for the last 4 days in multiple trees. Since all of it is e2e verifiable it basically builds itself. Codex even signs up for the services automatically via browser/computer use. My main job is adding credit card details and closing things that I don't see as a fit.

大家往 https://t.co/qUxn0LF7Ct 提的 Issues 和 PR 太多了，我几乎已经跟不上实现、测试、合并的节奏。

**Codex** 现在跑在 crabbox 里面，一边构建 crabbox，一边自己参与构建。
这已经快成我工作里的关键基础设施了。

过去 4 天里，**Codex** 一直在多个代码树里不停 loop。因为这些东西都能做 e2e 验证，基本上已经接近自己把自己搭起来了。它甚至会通过 browser/computer use 自动去注册各种服务。我的主要工作，反而变成填信用卡信息，以及把我觉得不合适的东西关掉。
